source.title: Contrastive-Based Deep Embeddings for Label Noise-Resilient Histopathology Image Classification
source.authors: Lucas Dedieu; Nicolas Nerrienet; A. Nivaggioli; Clara Simmat; Marceau Clavel; Arnaud Gauthier; Stéphane Sockeel; Rémy Peyret

record.tranche_reason: The study trains classifiers with synthetic label noise and measures test accuracy, but does not use the original study's random-label memorization measurement.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracies under synthetic label noise. It does not report training error on corrupted labels, so its results cannot establish perfect training fit. It does not test shuffled or Gaussian inputs, regularization's effect on random-label fitting, or the order in which real and random labels are learned.
record.test_reason: The study takes noisy-label overfitting as motivation and evaluates mitigation through clean-test accuracy. It reports neither training fit to corrupted labels nor memorization dynamics. Test accuracy under noise alone does not establish V4's joint claim of perfect training fit and steadily worsening generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that linear classifiers trained on contrastive embeddings improve robustness to synthetic label noise relative to image-based methods and non-contrastive embeddings, with weaker stability on smaller datasets and greater difficulty under asymmetric noise.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains linear classifiers on pretrained embeddings or image-based models using synthetic label noise; it does not reproduce random-label memorization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, embedding backbone, noise rate, and noise type affect reported test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: On NCT-CRC-HE-100k, baseline test accuracy falls from 96.7±0.1% at uniform noise η=0 to 35.5±0.3% at η=0.8. Contrastive embedding classifiers generally retain higher test accuracy under noise. These are generalization and mitigation results without measurements of corrupted-label training fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Histopathology classifiers trained on frozen contrastive embeddings generally retain better clean-test accuracy under synthetic label noise than the tested image-based and non-contrastive embedding methods.

record.problems: The study uses synthetic label noise; it notes lower stability on smaller datasets and greater difficulty resisting asymmetric noise. The supplied Table 2 and Table 3 text is garbled, preventing reliable attribution of many values to dataset and noise-rate conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted. Tables 2 and 3 are flattened and garbled in the supplied text, and the study does not report training error on noisy labels, which is required to assess the full V4 claim.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Perfect training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian augmentation of embeddings does not test this.

Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep and its relationship to test error approaching chance. The study measures only test accuracy, uses early stopping for the baseline, and does not reach completely random labels.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Whether networks learn shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise; no corresponding training trajectories are reported.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the reader's V4 limits_scope verdict: unreported training fit is an untested component, not evidence limiting the claim. Tables 2 and 3 and their omission are already declared in rows_left_out; no additional missing result is identified. Several Table 2 sequences, including the NCT-CRC-HE-100k results, are readable despite the flattened layout.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random labels to near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters; test error at chance.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.

The study reports test accuracy as label-noise rate varies, but does not report training accuracy or establish perfect training fit. Detailed table values are not extracted because the supplied table layout is too garbled to reliably associate values with all dataset and noise-rate conditions.
Whether weight decay, dropout or augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization when removed.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: synthetic uniform and asymmetric label noise in the tested histopathology datasets
reader_labels.reason: Test accuracy varies with noise rate, but the study does not report whether training error remains zero; the supplied table layout prevents reliable extraction of condition-specific values.
